en.title: Compress Consecutive Ranges in a Sorted List
en.description:
Given a strictly increasing list of integers, output each maximal run of consecutive integers as a to b, and output a single-element run as just that element. Runs keep their original order.

See the input protocol for this site's supplements to missing ranges and its recovery of typos in the source.
en.input: The first line contains n, followed by n strictly increasing integers. The original gave no numeric bounds; this site adds 0≤n≤100000 and −10^9≤a[i]≤10^9. An empty list produces empty output text.
en.output: Output one line per maximal consecutive run: a single item is written as a, and two or more items as a to b. An empty list produces empty output text.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 1 to 3 / 6 / 8 to 10; -2 to 0 / 2; empty text. Verified by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Keep the start and end of the current run; if the next value equals end+1, extend the run; otherwise close the current run and start a new one.
